The places where humanity lives were never designed to think.

Until now, spaces have functioned as passive structures⁠—fragmented, reactive, and disconnected systems that respond too late to the problems they could have anticipated, optimized, or prevented. Security is often reactive. Energy is frequently inefficient. Infrastructure remains opaque. Coordination is slow.
But the foundations of the physical world are changing.

Advances in artificial intelligence, edge computing, embedded sensing, connectivity and distributed systems are making it possible for physical environments to understand and respond to the world around them in real time.
For the first time, environments can evolve from static structures into adaptive systems.
Rh45 exists because this transition is no longer theoretical.

As populations expand and environments become more complex, the places where people live, work and gather must evolve from static containers into intelligent systems⁠—capable of understanding context, adapting to change and acting in real time to protect and improve human life.

We believe intelligence should not live only in screens, dashboards or isolated applications. It should be embedded in the environments themselves⁠—distributed across the physical world where life actually happens, and designed to operate responsibly, securely, and with human oversight.
Rh45 exists to give the physical world the ability to think: to make environments capable of sensing, reasoning, coordinating and acting⁠—autonomously, safely and under human governance.
We do not add technology for its own sake. We design environments that work with the people who inhabit them.

Places that protect.
Places that adapt.
Places that learn.
Places that evolve.
This is the future of living.
